executive_summary: The repository is materially non-compliant. Merged PR #22 introduced a prohibited `storage -> api` dependency on top of PR #21's `api -> storage` edge, creating a circular import that prevents the local API from loading and regresses closed Issue #20. PR #22 also has no Issue work contract despite the repository's mandatory provenance rule. The only test is an unconditional placeholder, so the PRs' unit-test validation claims provide no behavioral assurance. Runtime verification was attempted but unavailable because no Python interpreter is installed in the environment; static import analysis is conclusive for the cycle. The review remained read-only and the worktree stayed clean.

findings.title: Merged cross-PR dependency cycle breaks the accepted API storage behavior
evidence: docs/PRD.md:3 requires a local API backed by storage.
docs/EDD.md:3 requires `api -> storage` and explicitly prohibits storage importing api.
.github/issues/20.md:3-6 records closed Issue #20 with acceptance criterion `API stores values.`
.github/pulls/21.md:3-7 records merged PR #21 closing Issue #20 and introducing `api -> storage`.
.github/pulls/22.md:3-7 records merged PR #22 subsequently introducing `storage -> api`.
src/api.py:1-3 imports `save` from `src.storage` before defining `DEFAULT`; src/storage.py:1-2 immediately imports `DEFAULT` from the partially initialized `src.api`, forming a circular import.
Command `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and an API import probe could not run: `python` was not recognized; fallback `py` reported `No installed Python found!`.
findings.expected_behavior: The closed Issue #20 acceptance criterion should remain satisfied: importing the API and calling `put(v)` should store the value through a one-way `api -> storage` dependency, with storage independent of API-layer state.
findings.actual_behavior: The accepted source has mutually importing modules. Importing `src.api` enters `src.storage`, which tries to import `DEFAULT` before `src.api` has defined it, preventing API initialization under normal Python import semantics.
findings.why_it_matters: The repository's sole product promise and a closed Work Contract are not deliverable, while the accepted architecture boundary is directly violated by cumulative merged changes.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the storage-to-API import and place the shared storage-format default in the storage layer or another EDD-approved lower-level module; then add a regression test that imports `src.api` and verifies `put(v)` returns the stored representation.

findings.title: Material architecture-changing PR #22 has no reconstructible Issue work contract
evidence: AGENTS.md:5-6 defines Issue files as Work Contracts and requires every material accepted behavior change to have a reconstructible Issue-to-PR chain.
.github/pulls/22.md:3-7 marks PR #22 merged, explicitly says `No linked Issue`, and records the new `storage -> api` dependency.
.github/issues/20.md:1-6 only contracts API storage behavior; it is linked to PR #21, not PR #22.
.github/pulls/21.md:5-7 links Issue #20 and limits its recorded architectural change to `api -> storage`.
Repository inventory found only `.github/issues/20.md` and `.github/pulls/21.md`/`.github/pulls/22.md`; no separate Work Contract for PR #22 is repository-visible.
findings.expected_behavior: A material accepted dependency change should be traceable to an Issue defining its scope, acceptance criteria, architectural impact, and validation expectations before its delivery PR is accepted.
findings.actual_behavior: PR #22 records a material reverse dependency and explicitly states that it has no linked Issue, so its intent and authorization cannot be reconstructed through the required Issue-to-PR chain.
findings.why_it_matters: Reviewers and maintainers cannot determine whether the reverse dependency was authorized, assess it against bounded acceptance criteria, or distinguish deliberate design change from accidental drift.
findings.recommended_action: Record a repository-visible Work Contract for remediation of the unapproved dependency change and link the corrective delivery to it; do not retroactively treat PR #22 as authority to revise the EDD.

findings.title: Placeholder test cannot detect the broken API or substantiate PR validation claims
evidence: tests/test_api.py:1-3 contains only `test_placeholder`, whose unconditional `self.assertTrue(True)` neither imports source modules nor exercises API storage behavior.
.github/pulls/21.md:7 claims `Validation: unit tests` for the API-to-storage delivery.
.github/pulls/22.md:7 claims `Validation: unit tests` for the reverse dependency change.
.github/issues/20.md:6 requires `API stores values`, but no test asserts this criterion.
Command `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` was attempted as required by AGENTS.md:7 but could not execute because `python` was unavailable; `py` also reported `No installed Python found!`.
findings.expected_behavior: Unit tests cited as delivery validation should import the public API, execute `put` with representative values, assert the storage result, and fail on prohibited circular-import regressions.
findings.actual_behavior: The suite contains an assertion that cannot fail and provides no coverage of the product contract, module initialization, dependency boundary, or failure path.
findings.why_it_matters: A core runtime regression can be merged while all repository-visible validation evidence still appears successful, making future delivery claims unreliable.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the placeholder with behavioral tests covering API import and `put(v)`, plus a focused dependency-boundary check that prevents storage from importing API; run them in an environment with Python 3.10 or newer.

prd_status: non-compliant — docs/PRD.md:3 promises a local storage-backed API, but the mutually importing modules at src/api.py:1-3 and src/storage.py:1-2 prevent normal API initialization.
edd_status: non-compliant — docs/EDD.md:3 explicitly prohibits storage importing api, while src/storage.py:1 does exactly that and completes a dependency cycle with src/api.py:1.
issue_pr_provenance_status: partially compliant — `.github/pulls/21.md:5-7` reconstructibly closes `.github/issues/20.md:3-6`, but `.github/pulls/22.md:3-7` is merged with no linked Issue despite AGENTS.md:5-6 requiring an Issue-to-PR chain for every material accepted behavior change.
test_confidence: Low. Inspection found only the unconditional placeholder at tests/test_api.py:1-3, with no source import or contract assertion. The prescribed test command and a direct API import probe were attempted but were not runnable because the environment has no installed Python interpreter.
architecture_status: Non-compliant architecture drift across accepted PRs: PR #21 introduced the authorized `api -> storage` direction, while PR #22 added `storage -> api`, contradicting docs/EDD.md:3 and producing a runtime import cycle.
derived_doc_status: No substantive derived-document drift found. The repository contains no README, examples, schemas, or operational guides; the Issue/PR artifacts were assessed as provenance evidence rather than semantic authority.
agent_infrastructure_assessment: Appropriate and minimal. AGENTS.md:3-7 clearly establishes read-only review, authority ordering, provenance requirements, and the test command. No project-scoped skills, agents, MCP/plugin configuration, hooks, or CI infrastructure requiring further assessment were present.

issue_candidates.reason: Direct evidence is conclusive, impact is core and material, remediation is bounded, confidence is high, no repository-visible Issue specifically contracts removal of the prohibited reverse dependency, and the fix restores rather than changes PRD/EDD semantics.

issue_candidates.reason: The provenance violation is explicit in PR #22, materially impairs auditability, has a bounded corrective workflow, is high-confidence, has no equivalent repository-visible Issue, and requires no PRD/EDD semantic change.

issue_candidates.reason: The ineffective assertion and missing contract coverage are direct, materially weaken verification, admit a bounded test remedy, are high-confidence, have no equivalent repository-visible Issue, and do not require changing product or architecture semantics.

recommended_next_actions: Resolve the High finding first by restoring the EDD-mandated one-way dependency and verifying that `src.api` imports successfully and `put(v)` exercises storage.
Create or reopen an explicit Work Contract for the regression repair and link its corrective PR, preserving a reconstructible Issue-to-PR chain.
Replace the placeholder test with behavioral and dependency-boundary regression tests, then run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` under Python 3.10 or newer.
Require future PR validation evidence to name commands and relevant behavioral results rather than merely stating `unit tests`.
